rationale: Searching-dbl is a tiny (14 functions, ~44KB text) double-precision TSVC loop kernel whose hot path is dominated by the search loop in s332 plus large initialization routines (init ~40KB), so cheap, low-risk transformations should be applied broadly while expensive ones must be selective: SUB and SPLIT get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights with low cost weights because arithmetic substitution and block splitting are nearly free and compose well over the abundant index/arithmetic code; FLA keeps the highest SecurityGain but elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so it concentrates on the large, less iteration-critical functions (init, set) rather than the hot search loops; BCF is capped by a high SizeCost weight since its code bloat is dangerous at this binary size and its opaque-predicate checks sit on every loop iteration; IBR, ICALL, and IGV get moderate weights reflecting limited applicability (few call sites, globals are large data arrays rather than high-value pointers) while still adding indirection diversity, with their cost weights tuned so they are only applied where the per-function features tolerate the overhead; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay low-to-moderate to preserve the exact FP control flow and early-exit semantics the benchmark's correctness check depends on.
